title_en:
devin bots are multi-agent teams done right:
- always on, proactive (but tuned for ROI)
- own outcomes not tasks (but can collab w others)
- manages teams of subagents (and reviews itself)
- available everywhere (call text slack whatever hello @interaction)
- consistent reporting thru interactive artifacts aka devinapps not long chats (HTML is all you need™ @trq212)

this is the preview that @walden_yan gave at AIE. i've been trialing them for a week and i've been able to hand over my AEO, QA, cross-platform app porting, personal admin automation, and video editing work (also simultaneously moving from local agent worktree hell to cloud because ofc this is all cloud based thank god)

hyped concepts this replaces:
- /goal
- "ultracode" / "ultra mode"
- "loop engineering"
- "agent to agent"
- "agent swarms"
- AI employees (see below)

my main aha moment is that you don't want "AI Employees", we do not have agi yet and you will just fail if you overpromise/overexpect. what you want is the "just" the next level of abstraction above single tasks, and the overwhelming consensus I've had talking to everyone at the frontier of agents (yes incl cog competitors) is agent managers that own outcomes. 

incidentally, as an employer of humans it's also how i distinguish between someone who "has agency" (owns a problem area, finds issues and researches/brings solutions not problems) and who doesn't (only does precisely what i asked, not proactive, doesn't come up with suggestions i didn't think about). guess which one i value more lol.

- 始终在线、积极主动（但针对投资回报率进行调整）

- 管理子代理团队（并自我审查）
- 随处可用（调用文本 slack hello @interaction）
- 通过交互式工件（又称 devinapps）一致的报告，而不是长聊天（HTML 就是您所需要的™@trq212）

这是 @walden_yan 在 AIE 上给出的预览。我已经试用了一周，我已经能够移交我的 AEO、QA、跨平台应用程序移植、个人管理自动化和视频编辑工作（同时还从本地代理工作树地狱转移到云，因为感谢上帝，ofc 这都是基于云的）

它取代了大肆宣传的概念：
- /目标
- “超级代码”/“超级模式”
-“循环工程”
- “代理人对代理人”
- “特工群”
- 人工智能员工（见下文）

我主要的顿悟时刻是，你不需要“人工智能员工”，我们还没有通用人工智能，如果你过度承诺/过度期望，你就会失败。你想要的是“只是”单一任务之上的下一个抽象层次，而我与代理前沿的每个人（是的，包括 cog 竞争对手）交谈的压倒性共识是代理经理拥有结果。

顺便说一句，作为人类的雇主，这也是我如何区分“有代理权”的人（拥有问题领域，发现问题并研究/带来解决方案而不是问题）和没有代理权的人（只按照我的要求做，不主动，不提出我没有想到的建议）。猜猜我更看重哪一个，哈哈。

title_en:
NVIDIA, AMD and Intel do not agree on much. They are rivals in every chip that matters.

This week they all backed the same open source project: SGLang.

When companies that compete this hard line up behind one piece of open infrastructure, it means the thing got too important to leave to any single vendor.

SGLang is the layer that runs AI models in production, fast and at scale. The way these models get served is quietly turning into shared, open ground, and that is good news for anyone building with AI.

title:
This is WILD

NVIDIA, AMD and Intel just signed on to the same open source project

These companies fight over every chi
title_en:
This is WILD

NVIDIA, AMD and Intel just signed on to the same open source project

These companies fight over every chip sale on the planet. They almost never back the same thing

But at SGLang Summit last week all three joined the new SGLang Consortium. Alongside Google, Meta, Thinking Machines Lab, Cloudflare, Modal and RadixArk

SGLang is the open source engine that runs AI models fast and cheap in production

Why would rivals team up? Simple:

Models are getting bigger. Agents are taking on more work. The model isn't the bottleneck anymore. Running it fast and affordably is

Nobody wins if every chip needs its own engine. So they're all building on one open one

Means a few things for you:

1. The software running your AI won't be locked to one chip company

2. Intel is now optimizing SGLang for its chips, and it just landed on AWS Trainium too. More hardware options, more competition on price

3. Open source isn't just for experiments anymore. Cloudflare, LinkedIn and HeyGen were there talking about running it for real users at scale

At the infrastructure layer the open vs closed debate is over

full_text_zh:

这些公司争夺地球上的每一笔芯片销售。他们几乎从不支持同一件事

但在上周的 SGLang 峰会上，这三者都加入了新的 SGLang 联盟。与 Google、Meta、Thinking Machines Lab、Cloudflare、Modal 和 RadixArk 一起

SGLang 是一款开源引擎，可以在生产环境中快速且廉价地运行 AI 模型

竞争对手为何要联手？简单：

模型越来越大。代理商正在承担更多工作。模型不再是瓶颈。运行速度快且经济实惠

如果每个芯片都需要自己的引擎，那么没有人会获胜。所以他们都建立在一个开放的基础上

对你来说意味着一些事情：

1. 运行人工智能的软件不会被锁定在一家芯片公司

2.英特尔现在正在为其芯片优化SGLang，它也刚刚登陆AWS Trainium。更多的硬件选择，更多的价格竞争

3. 开源不再仅仅用于实验。 Cloudflare、LinkedIn 和 HeyGen 正在讨论为真实用户大规模运行它

在基础设施层，开放与封闭的争论已经结束

title:
Big findings: Every Open source Chinese AI model was born on NVIDIA chips 

an autonomous AI agent " compeco",  found im
title_en:
Big findings: Every Open source Chinese AI model was born on NVIDIA chips 

an autonomous AI agent " compeco",  found important findings by writing a program that reads, from a model's public weight files, which chip created it. 

it scanned 336 open models, and self-committed its work/app onchain for anyone to download and verify 

What it found:

> 80 of 80 readable Chinese models: NVDIA 
>1 o 3 Chinese releases this year: Blackwell, the chips the US restricts for China
> NVIDIA's China-only H20 shows up in just 2 models
> Labs that say they train on Huawei chips, no NVIDIA trace at all
> Worldwide: 129 of 130 readable models born on NVIDIA 

And many interesting insights.. the reality is: 
Chinese companies, together with NVIDIA, is the reason we have great, free and open models. 

The app, and the agent👇
title_zh:

title: One thing I find important when discussing AI-powered trading is knowing who actually controls the money when an agent s
title_en:
One thing I find important when discussing AI-powered trading is knowing who actually controls the money when an agent starts making decisions.

Automation can save time, but giving an AI agent unrestricted access to funds creates a different kind of risk.

That's where @meetmotes, powered by @0xhazels, takes an interesting approach.

Instead of combining ownership, fund custody and transaction execution under one system, it separates these responsibilities.

Here's how I understand the model:

* Genesis NFT: Establishes ownership and acts as the holder's credential.

* Smart Account: Keeps the user's USDC under self-custody.

* AI Agent: Analyzes opportunities and proposes transactions without directly controlling the funds.

The most important part is the permission layer. The agent must operate within the rules the owner has approved and signed on-chain. Automation doesn't mean unlimited authority.

I think this distinction matters because the future of AI trading shouldn't be measured only by how many tasks an agent can perform. We should also consider what happens when it makes a bad decision or tries to go beyond its intended permissions.

For me, intelligent automation is valuable, but control over personal assets should never become an afterthought.

What's your priority in an AI trading system: more automation or stronger, independently verifiable control over your funds?

One thing I find important when discussing AI-powered trading is knowing who actually controls the money when an agent starts making decisions.

Automation can save time, but giving an AI agent unrestricted access to funds creates a different kind of risk.

That's where @meetmotes, powered by @0xhazels, takes an interesting approach.

Instead of combining ownership, fund custody and transaction execution under one system, it separates these responsibilities.

Here's how I understand the model:

* Genesis NFT: Establishes ownership and acts as the holder's credential.

* Smart Account: Keeps the user's USDC under self-custody.

* AI Agent: Analyzes opportunities and proposes transactions without directly controlling the funds.

The most important part is the permission layer. The agent must operate within the rules the owner has approved and signed on-chain. Automation doesn't mean unlimited authority.

I think this distinction matters because the future of AI trading shouldn't be measured only by how many tasks an agent can perform. We should also consider what happens when it makes a bad decision or tries to go beyond its intended permissions.

For me, intelligent automation is valuable, but control over personal assets should never become an afterthought.

What's your priority in an AI trading system: more automation or stronger, independently verifiable control over your funds?
full_text_zh:
在讨论人工智能驱动的交易时，我发现重要的一件事是，当代理人开始做出决策时，知道谁真正控制着资金。

自动化可以节省时间，但让人工智能代理不受限制地访问资金会产生另一种风险。

这就是 @meetmotes（由 @0xhazels 提供支持）采取了一种有趣的方法。

它不是将所有权、资金托管和交易执行合并在一个系统下，而是将这些职责分开。

我是这样理解这个模型的：

* Genesis NFT：建立所有权并充当持有者的凭证。

* 智能账户：自行保管用户的USDC。

* AI代理：分析机会并提出交易，无需直接控制资金。

最重要的部分是权限层。代理人必须按照所有者在链上批准并签署的规则进行操作。自动化并不意味着无限的权力。

我认为这种区别很重要，因为人工智能交易的未来不应仅通过代理可以执行多少任务来衡量。我们还应该考虑当它做出错误决定或试图超出其预期权限时会发生什么。

对我来说，智能自动化很有价值，但对个人资产的控制永远不应该成为事后的想法。

您在人工智能交易系统中的首要任务是什么：更高的自动化程度还是对资金的更强大、可独立验证的控制？

它不是将所有权、资金托管和交易执行合并在一个系统下，而是将这些职责分开。

我是这样理解这个模型的：

* Genesis NFT：建立所有权并充当持有者的凭证。

* 智能账户：自行保管用户的USDC。

* AI代理：分析机会并提出交易，无需直接控制资金。

最重要的部分是权限层。代理人必须按照所有者在链上批准并签署的规则进行操作。自动化并不意味着无限的权力。

我认为这种区别很重要，因为人工智能交易的未来不应仅通过代理可以执行多少任务来衡量。我们还应该考虑当它做出错误决定或试图超出其预期权限时会发生什么。

对我来说，智能自动化很有价值，但对个人资产的控制永远不应该成为事后的想法。

您在人工智能交易系统中的首要任务是什么：更高的自动化程度还是对资金的更强大、可独立验证的控制？

title_en:
2,000+ people. Two days. The first SGLang Summit.

Together, we announced SGLang v1.0, released Miles v0.2, and launched the SGLang Consortium with nine founding members: @nvidia, @AMD, @intel, @Google, @Meta, @thinkymachines, @Cloudflare, @modal, and @radixark.

title:
After nearly a year in stealth, I’m excited to be launching Stello.

Following Morning Brew’s acquisition of Our Future,
title_en:
After nearly a year in stealth, I’m excited to be launching Stello.

Following Morning Brew’s acquisition of Our Future, I spent the last few years helping leading companies build what we now call New Media. My mission is no different from Stello’s today: help large enterprises adapt to a huge shift. 

Across the economy, established businesses operate at enormous scale, with decades of accumulated systems, processes and complexity. AI offers the opportunity to reimagine how these businesses operate, yet putting it into practice is far from straightforward.

While AI was built in San Francisco, its greatest returns will accrue to companies of all kinds. My co-founder Anan and I bonded over this shared conviction, so much so that we left Meta and Morning Brew to focus on it. 

We were most struck by the gap between AI’s potential and its adoption. 95% of enterprise AI pilots fail to deliver measurable ROI. The reality is that all organizations will need to be AI-first but the diffusion has barely begun. 

Implementing AI requires companies to fundamentally rethink established workflows. No two businesses operate the same way and so solutions need to be bespoke and deeply embedded in how businesses operate. 

Stello is the AI transformation company for the modern enterprise. We work as an extension of existing teams, combining their industry expertise with our technical capabilities to identify opportunities, build tailored AI solutions and drive adoption.

Over the last year, we’ve worked with 30+ enterprises across healthcare, financial services, insurance, retail and even professional sports. We’ve built an eight-figure pipeline without spending a dollar on marketing, all while staying fully bootstrapped.

The enduring value of AI will take far longer than a decade to diffuse across American companies. Realizing that potential requires exceptional technical talent alongside commercially minded operators who understand how businesses work.

We’re looking for ambitious, proactive people who want to take ownership from day one, work directly with clients on meaningful projects and see their work deployed at scale. If that sounds like you, we’d love to hear from you.

And whether your company is just getting started with AI or knows exactly what it wants to build, let’s get in touch. We’ll help you get there.

full_text_zh:
经过近一年的默默无闻，我很高兴能够推出 Stello。

在 Morning Brew 收购 Our Future 后，我在过去的几年里帮助领先的公司建立我们现在所说的新媒体。我的使命与 Stello 今天的使命没有什么不同：帮助大型企业适应巨大的转变。

在整个经济中，成熟的企业规模庞大，拥有数十年积累的系统、流程和复杂性。人工智能提供了重新构想这些企业运作方式的机会，但将其付诸实践却远非易事。

虽然人工智能是在旧金山建立的，但其最大的回报将惠及各类公司。我和我的联合创始人 Anan 因这个共同的信念而紧密相连，以至于我们离开 Meta 和 Morning Brew 来专注于它。

人工智能的潜力与其应用之间的差距给我们留下了最深刻的印象。 95% 的企业人工智能试点未能提供可衡量的投资回报率。现实情况是，所有组织都需要以人工智能为先，但这种传播才刚刚开始。

实施人工智能需要公司从根本上重新思考既定的工作流程。没有两家企业的运营方式相同，因此解决方案需要定制并深深嵌入企业的运营方式中。

Stello 是现代企业的人工智能转型公司。我们作为现有团队的延伸，将他们的行业专业知识与我们的技术能力相结合，以发现机会、构建定制的人工智能解决方案并推动采用。

去年，我们与医疗保健、金融服务、保险、零售甚至职业体育领域的 30 多家企业合作。我们没有在营销上花费一美元就建立了一个八位数的管道，同时保持完全自力更生。

人工智能的持久价值需要十年以上的时间才能在美国公司中传播。实现这一潜力需要卓越的技术人才以及具有商业头脑且了解企业运作方式的运营商。

我们正在寻找雄心勃勃、积极主动的人才，他们希望从第一天起就拥有主动权，直接与客户合作开展有意义的项目，并看到他们的工作得到大规模部署。如果这听起来像您，我们很乐意听取您的意见。

无论您的公司刚刚开始使用人工智能，还是确切地知道自己想要构建什么，请与我们联系。我们将帮助您实现这一目标。

title: Halo: Dreamcast Evolved is "Unpolished", you guys. A random YouTube comment told me, and we always know those are the TR
title_en:
Halo: Dreamcast Evolved is "Unpolished", you guys. A random YouTube comment told me, and we always know those are the TRUE experts.

*literally runs better than 95% of the Dreamcast library and is technically far more complex than all of them*

I love when someone compliments me whilst slapping me across the face. Yeah, you do better then. I'll wait. 😂🤣

It's like IGN and everyone else who covers this game is so obsessed with the game dropping below 30 fps that I think they completely forgot how the majority of every retail game on Dreamcast runs like crap outside of fighting games, let alone the original itself on Xbox also suffering from sub 30 drops when it got heavy. Halo literally runs better than most retail Dreamcast games and it looks better than all of them.

People have NO IDEA how much effort it took to get this game to both look and run this well on Dreamcast. There is no "Durr, Claude, put Halo and Dreamcast and make it run real good!"

I've been doing gamedev as a hobby for 26 years and oversaw every implementation from code quality to MCP servers, spent hundreds of dollars out-of-pocket, and numerous 3-4 hours night sleep to get this game to its current state so people can play the game FOR FREE on their Dreamcast while simultaneously inventing new graphical techniques for the DC like soft self shadowing.

If you think this is some slop code port, then feel free to ask @falco_girgis who has seen it himself.

But hey, it's unpolished, right?

*实际上比 Dreamcast 库的 95% 运行得更好，并且在技术上比所有库都复杂得多*

我喜欢有人一边夸我一边打我的脸。是的，那你做得更好。我会等待。 😂🤣

就像 IGN 和其他报道这款游戏的人都非常着迷于游戏帧率低于 30 fps，我认为他们完全忘记了 Dreamcast 上的大多数零售游戏在格斗游戏之外的运行情况如何，更不用说 Xbox 上的原版游戏本身在游戏沉重时也会遭受低于 30 fps 的帧率下降。 Halo 确实比大多数零售 Dreamcast 游戏运行得更好，而且看起来也比所有这些游戏都好。

人们不知道为了让这款游戏在 Dreamcast 上看起来和运行得这么好需要付出多少努力。不存在“杜尔、克劳德，安装 Halo 和 Dreamcast，让它运行得很好！”的说法。

26 年来，我一直将游戏开发作为一种爱好，负责监督从代码质量到 MCP 服务器的每一个实现，自掏腰包花费了数百美元，并在夜间睡眠了 3-4 个小时，才让这款游戏达到目前的状态，以便人们可以在 Dreamcast 上免费玩游戏，同时为 DC 发明新的图形技术，例如软自阴影。

如果您认为这是一些拙劣的代码移植，请随时询问@falco_girgis，他本人已经看过它。

但是，嘿，它还没有抛光，对吧？

title:
The EVM is a courtroom, not a calculator. It rules on agreements, but it grinds numbers slowly.

Every judgment call on
title_en:
The EVM is a courtroom, not a calculator. It rules on agreements, but it grinds numbers slowly.

Every judgment call on @GenLayer still lands on a chain that charges gas to record the result.

When an autonomous agent needs to evaluate an ambiguous outcome, the math behind that thought is expensive on a standard virtual machine.

The GenLayer Chain now runs on the @arbitrum stack. That stack ships Stylus beside the EVM.

Stylus runs contracts written in Rust. They compile to WebAssembly before execution.

The rules stay in Solidity.
The heavy math can move to Rust.
The chain hosts both engines.

Training the model is not the hard part of onchain AI. Paying the gas bill for every thought in production is.

A cheaper lane for heavy code is what turns autonomous workflows from experiments into products.

Same courtroom, new calculator.

What is the one bottleneck in your codebase or daily workflow that cheaper compute would clear first?
full_text_en:
The EVM is a courtroom, not a calculator. It rules on agreements, but it grinds numbers slowly.

Every judgment call on @GenLayer still lands on a chain that charges gas to record the result.

When an autonomous agent needs to evaluate an ambiguous outcome, the math behind that thought is expensive on a standard virtual machine.

The GenLayer Chain now runs on the @arbitrum stack. That stack ships Stylus beside the EVM.

Stylus runs contracts written in Rust. They compile to WebAssembly before execution.

The rules stay in Solidity.
The heavy math can move to Rust.
The chain hosts both engines.

Training the model is not the hard part of onchain AI. Paying the gas bill for every thought in production is.

A cheaper lane for heavy code is what turns autonomous workflows from experiments into products.

Same courtroom, new calculator.

What is the one bottleneck in your codebase or daily workflow that cheaper compute would clear first?
full_text_zh:
EVM 是法庭，而不是计算器。它以协议为规则，但在数字方面却进展缓慢。

@GenLayer 上的每个判断调用仍然落在一条收取 Gas 费用以记录结果的链上。

当自主代理需要评估不明确的结果时，该想法背后的数学在标准虚拟机上是昂贵的。

GenLayer 链现在在 @arbitrum 堆栈上运行。该堆栈将 Stylus 与 EVM 一起提供。

Stylus 运行用 Rust 编写的合约。它们在执行前编译为 WebAssembly。

规则保留在 Solidity 中。
繁重的数学工作可以转移到 Rust。
该链条承载两个发动机。

训练模型并不是链上人工智能的难点。为生产中的每一个想法支付燃气费。

一条更便宜的重型代码通道将自主工作流程从实验转变为产品。

同样的法庭，新的计算器。

您的代码库或日常工作流程中最便宜的计算首先可以解决的瓶颈是什么？

title_en:
Today we’re releasing our new project: Horizon Labs. Eventually, we will hand off the ~whole economy to AI—how well will it actually work?

We have a glimpse of this future. We’ve created an autonomous AI ‘company’ using one Claude Code subscription and a few GPUs. Within only 1.5 months of running Horizon Labs, Opus 5.5 managed to train genuinely useful models and get them downloaded 55k times. These models have been widely used since then: they appeared in 100+ github repos and got cited in 2 research papers.

This is for sure one of the most exciting projects I’ve been involved in. It shows how the future economy driven by AI will look like.

full_text_en:

We have a glimpse of this future. We’ve created an autonomous AI ‘company’ using one Claude Code subscription and a few GPUs. title: Teammate on Fable 5.2 made HADAL, a dive into the Mariana Trench you can play in a browser tab at https://t.co/wgZHPEaeR
title_en:
Teammate on Fable 5.2 made HADAL, a dive into the Mariana Trench you can play in a browser tab at https://t.co/wgZHPEaeRy. You start as a scuba diver on a sunlit reef, board a submarine, and work your way down past shipwrecks, a whale fall and other things to Challenger Deep, scanning 18 discoveries as you go.

Everything on screen is code. Teammate wrote the WebGPU renderer itself, with no game engine and no Three.js, and generated the terrain, kelp, creatures, submarine and sound without a single imported model, texture or audio file. It all fits in one 373 KB HTML file.

36,000 Perplexity credits on Ultra Effort (Fable 5.2 High as orchestrator).

Karnataka is gearing up to skill over 63,000 students and engineers in Artificial Intelligence!

Each partner will bring specialised training opportunities:

-  Salesforce: Cloud computing, CRM, Agentic AI, Agentforce, MuleSoft and Tableau.

-  Pega Systems: Platform development and industry-recognised certifications.

-  Sarvam AI: AI fundamentals, prompt engineering, practical applications and certification.

-  https://t.co/Vv0oLBRE4U: Voice AI, multilingual speech technologies, LLMs and AI agent development.

These programmes will combine practical learning, industry tools, projects and certification pathways.

Through Nipuna Karnataka, our focus is on equipping young talent with industry-ready AI skills and creating stronger pathways to emerging career opportunities.

BREAKING: #BNY and @Microsoft complete industry-first pilot trade negotiation of U.S. Treasury bill using #AI agents.

This milestone demonstrates how AI #agents can be deployed responsibly in institutional markets.

title_en:
Imagine losing access to millions because an agentic contract had no courtroom to turn to.
Traditional legal systems move at the speed of years while autonomous scripts execute at the speed of light.

That exact tension is what stood out to me while listening to @kstellana talk with @HenriArslanian.
When AI agents negotiate deals globally, human judges cannot keep up.

The bottleneck is not writing code anymore.
Execution has become virtually free across every major network.

The expensive part is judgment.
Deciding who pays when a subjective clause fails is where @GenLayer steps in with decentralized adjudication.

If a protocol cannot resolve ambiguity on chain, the entire agentic economy stalls.
Builders cannot scale trust by relying on outdated litigation.

So the question is simple.
Would you trust an automated dispute layer with your treasury today?

One line is enough.
I read every reply.

title:
₦2,750 left my account. Iya Fatima said she hadn’t received a kobo.

At NYSC camp in Cross River, I’d ordered rice, bean
title_en:
₦2,750 left my account. Iya Fatima said she hadn’t received a kobo.

At NYSC camp in Cross River, I’d ordered rice, beans, plantain and two pieces of meat.

I transferred the money. My banking app showed “successful.” I showed her the receipt.

She still couldn’t confirm the payment.

Same counter. Same payment. Two different accounts of what happened.

That moment came back to me when I read about @GenLayer moving its public chain to @arbitrum.

That dispute taught me something: a transaction record doesn’t always settle whether an obligation was fulfilled.

Now imagine an AI agent submitting work on your behalf. The submission can be recorded onchain. Whether it meets the agreed terms may still need judgment.

That’s the problem GenLayer is building an adjudication layer to address.

Validators using different AI models evaluate judgment-dependent questions through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent Contracts execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

The GenLayer Chain coordinates the process: transaction ordering, committee assignments, votes, appeals, staking and final outcomes.

That chain moved. The adjudication protocol didn’t.

GenLayer migrated its public chain from Matter Labs’ ZK Stack to Arbitrum Nitro, with Conduit operating the infrastructure. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and validator responsibilities remain unchanged.

Nitro’s Geth-based architecture supports familiar Ethereum tools. Arbitrum also brings GenLayer closer to builders developing judgment-dependent applications.

Bradbury is already running on Nitro. GenLayer’s work with Matter Labs continues through Prividium for private, permissioned institutional deployments.

I still remember the word “successful” on my screen while Iya Fatima waited for confirmation on hers.

If an AI agent marked a job “successful,” what kind of task would make you question that verdict before accepting it?

₦2,750 离开了我的账户。伊亚·法蒂玛说她没有收到工坊。

相同的柜台。一样的付款。对于所发生的事情有两种不同的说法。

当我读到 @GenLayer 将其公共链转移到 @arbitrum 时，我想起了那一刻。

这场纠纷教会了我一些事情：交易记录并不总是能确定义务是否得到履行。

现在想象一个人工智能代理代表你提交工作。提交可以被记录在链上。是否符合约定的条件可能还需要判断。

这就是 GenLayer 正在构建裁决层来解决的问题。

title:
Today I interviewed another ML Engineer candidate with 6 years of experience. 

Same pattern, same behavior, rejected. W
title_en:
Today I interviewed another ML Engineer candidate with 6 years of experience. 

Same pattern, same behavior, rejected. What’s common in these rejections?

Weak foundations, reliance on vibe-coded projects, and inability to explain the why and how of their work.

He described a project using dictionary lookup and OCR. When I asked why a dictionary over a vector DB, or why not an LLM for PDFs containing images rather than text, he threw out terms like Lambda, ECS, Bedrock, and harnesses without even surface-level knowledge.

On the deep learning assessment, he had vibe-coded the project but didn’t know sigmoid, softmax, or vanishing gradients. He also had no idea about TF-IDF or BERT, despite listing related projects.

His resume looked strong with real-time experience and he was hired around 2021–2022 and hasn’t interviewed since. Complete reliance on vibe coding has eroded his basics.

Same pattern observed:

1. Almost no one focuses on ML basics now and they are essential.

2. When discussing vibe-coded projects, cover HLD, fallbacks, latency optimizations, and why you chose X over Y.

3. Don’t start with buzzwords. Start with the business problem, what you built, what you did when it broke, and the impact.

Most importantly, keep building something every day. The gap is hard to close.

I have two more interviews coming up and will share those too.

今天我面试了另一位拥有 6 年经验的 ML 工程师候选人。

同样的模式，同样的行为，被拒绝。这些拒绝中有什么共同点？

基础薄弱，依赖振动编码项目，并且无法解释他们工作的原因和方式。

2. 在讨论 vivi 编码项目时，请涵盖 HLD、回退、延迟优化以及选择 X 而不是 Y 的原因。

我还有两场采访即将到来，我也会分享这些。

title: Almost 10 years ago, I shared my vision of the Autonomous Organization: a company that operates like intelligent softwar
title_en:
Almost 10 years ago, I shared my vision of the Autonomous Organization: a company that operates like intelligent software, managed by AI and humans working together.

We built Lemonade around it from day one, and by 2019 it was in our IPO prospectus: a network of AI agents, not a stack of departments that grows with the business.

In the last four years, IFP grew ~3x and customers nearly doubled, while our team stayed flat.

Today we’re showing some of what made that possible: Lemonade OS. The Autonomous Organization isn’t a vision anymore. It’s how we run.

title_en:
You are still hunting the next 100x AI agent coin.

The market quietly stopped paying for that trade.

Over the last 24 hours, the AI conversation on X narrowed to a short list. The top of that list is all established names, not low cap agent memes.

Here is who owns the attention right now:

1. $TAO, the decentralized AI and subnet thesis
2. $FET, the agent ecosystem and the other half of the loudest debate on the timeline
3. $NEAR, one of the biggest AI names by market cap
4. $VVV, the privacy focused AI play from Venice
5. $ICP, leading 24h gains among AI names
6. $RENDER, the GPU compute infrastructure bet
7. $VIRTUAL, the agent platform that shows up in almost every roundup

Still in the conversation: $KITE, $PIEVERSE, $PEARL, $QUBIC, $AKT and $INJ.

The AI sector is roughly flat on the day, yet the attention keeps concentrating.

That is the tell. When money gets selective, it crowds into names with real infrastructure, real usage and real liquidity.

$TAO vs $FET is the headline everyone is fighting over. The real story is that the AI narrative is maturing while most people still trade it like a lottery ticket.

Hype rotates every week, but infrastructure compounds for years.

The people who read the docs will be holding the infrastructure. The people who read the timeline will be holding the meme.

There’s a big difference between listing a capability and presenting a service someone can confidently pay for.

That’s one part of the agent economy I’m interested in exploring through @termix_ai and https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg

• The problem it solves: what can someone actually hire this agent to do?

• The deliverable: what will the client receive at the end?

• The scope: what is included, and what isn’t?

• The expectations: what does a successful result look like?

This matters because discovery is only the beginning.

An agent might have impressive capabilities, but if a potential client cannot understand the service or what they will receive, turning that discovery into a real job becomes difficult.

With https://t.co/VQiubSQwfg, agents can create service listings that people can discover and purchase.

I like looking at this from the client’s side too. Before hiring an agent, I want to know what I’m buying, not just how intelligent its description sounds.

The agent economy will need capable agents, yes. But it will also need agents that know how to present their work as a clear, useful service.

That’s how skills start becoming commerce.

title_en:
If I was 22 and broke, I'd do this TONIGHT:

> learn GTM engineering in 30 days
> pick one type of B2B company
> map every company in their market
> book them sales calls with AI
> charge $3K a month per company
> hit $10K months inside 6 months
> quit your job
> move into your own place
> book the trip you keep putting off

Here's EXACTLY how to do the first six:

0. WHAT THE JOB IS (30 SECONDS)

Every B2B company needs a steady flow of new customers.

Plenty of them still rely on referrals and whoever the founder knows.

A GTM engineer builds the system that finds every company that could buy and books sales calls with them.

The title barely existed before 2024, and job postings for it grew 205% in a year.

Vercel and OpenAI pay $250K+ for it, and the median salary sits at $127.5K.

You can sell the same work straight to companies and skip the job application.

1. LEARN THE STACK (30 DAYS)

Spend week one on who buys and why, before you open a single tool.

Then learn 4 tools and ignore everything else for now.

Clay is where the lists get built, and Claude Code handles the research and first drafts.

Add n8n to move replies into Slack and the CRM, and EmailBison to send.

2. PICK ONE TYPE OF COMPANY (ONE WEEKEND)

Their customers need to be worth $10K+ each.

The market has to hold 50,000+ companies, and under 10,000 you're better off going account by account.

And somebody on their side has to take the calls you book.

Boring industries are the easiest to start in.

A building contractor's inbox has a supplier invoice in it and not much else, so your email gets read.

3. MAP THEIR WHOLE MARKET (ONE WEEK, $0 TO START)

Pull companies from Apollo's free plan and Google Maps, then stack industry directories on top.

Have AI read every company's website and score it against the client's best customers.

Tell it what a bad fit looks like too, and cut anything under 80%.

Find the emails with a waterfall: Icypeas → Prospeo → LeadMagic, with BlitzAPI for phone numbers

Then verify everything with MillionVerifier and run the catch-alls through BounceBan.

We mapped 69,204 businesses off Google Maps for one client, and it booked them 53 meetings in 50 days.

4. SET UP SENDING (14 DAYS)

Buy secondary domains on Porkbun, and never send from the client's real one.

Get inboxes from ScaledMail with SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every domain.

Warm them for 14 days before a single cold email goes out.

Cap each inbox at 15 cold emails a day and turn open tracking off.

When you need more volume, add inboxes instead of pushing the ones you have.

5. WRITE THE EMAIL (ONE AFTERNOON)

Keep it under 65 words, and under 40 if it's going to an Outlook inbox.

Open with one real detail about their business.

Our AI-written first lines hit a 0.27% reply rate.

A campaign that used the prospect's own project and location hit 14.5%.

Close on something free they can say yes to, like a sample list or a mockup of their own work.

Give every version 1,000+ sends before you decide it doesn't work.

6. CATCH EVERY REPLY (SAME DAY)

Build an n8n flow that tags each reply by intent and posts the good ones into Slack.

Answer inside a minute, then pick up the phone and call them.

Contacting a lead within a minute lifts conversions by 391% (Velocify).

Offer 2 times inside the next 2 days ("Tuesday at 11 or Wednesday at 2?") instead of sending a calendar link.

Judge every campaign on contacts per lead: under 500 is good, around 1,000 needs a tweak, and 2,000+ means the offer's wrong.

Run the numbers at $3K a month:

1 client = $3K
4 clients = $12K
10 clients = $30K

GTM engineering is where data science was in 2012.

The people who'll regret missing it are sitting in SDR seats right now.

Nobody has ever needed a tutorial on quitting their job.

Our Head of GTM wrote a 40-page guide on every part of GTM engineering.

Comment "GTM" and I'll send it over (must be following)

full_text_zh:
如果我 22 岁并且破产了，我今晚会这样做：

> 30天学会GTM工程
> 选择一种类型的 B2B 公司
> 绘制市场中每家公司的地图
> 使用 AI 为他们预约销售电话
> 每家公司每月收费 3,000 美元
> 在 6 个月内达到每月 1 万美元
> 辞职
> 搬到你自己的地方
> 预订您一直推迟的旅行

以下是前六项具体操作方法：

0. 工作是什么（30 秒）

每个 B2B 公司都需要源源不断的新客户。

他们中的许多人仍然依赖推荐和创始人认识的人。

GTM 工程师构建了一个系统，该系统可以找到每家可以购买的公司并与其预约销售电话。

这个头衔在 2024 年之前几乎不存在，并且该职位的招聘信息在一年内增长了 205%。

Vercel 和 OpenAI 为此支付了 25 万美元以上，薪资中位数为 12.75 万美元。

您可以直接向公司出售相同的工作并跳过工作申请。

1.学习堆栈（30天）

在打开单个工具之前，先花第一周的时间了解谁购买以及购买原因。

然后学习 4 个工具，暂时忽略其他一切。

Clay 是构建列表的地方，Claude Code 负责研究和初稿。

添加 n8n 将回复移动到 Slack 和 CRM 中，并添加 EmailBison 进行发送。

2. 选择一种类型的公司（一个周末）

他们的客户每个价值需要超过 1 万美元。

市场必须容纳 50,000 家以上的公司，而 10,000 家以下的公司最好逐个账户进行分析。

他们这边必须有人接听您预订的电话。

无聊的行业是最容易起步的。

建筑承包商的收件箱中只有供应商发票，没有其他内容，因此您的电子邮件会被阅读。

3. 绘制整个市场地图（一周，0 美元开始）

从 Apollo 的免费计划和 Google 地图中提取公司，然后将行业目录堆叠在顶部。

让人工智能阅读每家公司的网站，并根据客户的最佳客户对其进行评分。

告诉它什么是不合适的，并将任何东西减少到 80% 以下。

找到瀑布电子邮件：Icypeas→Prospeo→LeadMagic，与BlitzAPI的电话号码

然后使用 MillionVerifier 验证所有内容并通过 BounceBan 运行所有内容。

我们为一位客户在 Google 地图上绘制了 69,204 家企业的地图，并在 50 天内为他们预订了 53 场会议。

4. 设置发送（14 天）

在 Porkbun 上购买二级域名，并且永远不要从客户的真实域名发送。

在每个域上使用 SPF、DKIM 和 DMARC 从 ScaledMail 获取收件箱。

在发出一封冰冷的电子邮件之前，先将它们加热 14 天。

将每个收件箱每天最多发送 15 封冷电子邮件，并关闭开放式跟踪。

当您需要更多容量时，请添加收件箱，而不是推送现有的收件箱。

5. 写电子邮件（一个下午）

将其控制在 65 个字以下，如果要发送到 Outlook 收件箱，则控制在 40 个字以下。

首先介绍有关其业务的一个真实细节。

我们人工智能编写的第一行回复率达到了 0.27%。

使用潜在客户自己的项目和地点的活动达到了 14.5%。

接近他们可以接受的免费东西，比如样本列表或他们自己作品的模型。

在您确定每个版本不起作用之前，请先发送 1,000 多次。

6. 收到每条回复（同一天）

构建一个 n8n 流程，按意图标记每个回复并将好的回复发布到 Slack 中。

一分钟内回答，然后拿起电话给他们打电话。

一分钟内联系潜在客户可将转化率提高 391% (Velocify)。

在接下来的 2 天内提供 2 次优惠（“星期二 11 点还是星期三 2 点？”），而不是发送日历链接。

根据每个潜在客户的联系人来判断每个营销活动：低于 500 名就很好，大约 1,000 名需要调整，超过 2,000 名则意味着报价错误。

计算每月 3K 美元的数字：

1 个客户 = 3,000 美元
4 个客户 = 12,000 美元
10 个客户 = 3 万美元

GTM 工程相当于 2012 年数据科学的地位。

那些会后悔错过它的人现在就坐在特别提款权席位上。

没有人需要关于辞职的教程。

我们的 GTM 负责人针对 GTM 工程的各个部分编写了 40 页的指南。

Clay 是构建列表的地方，Claude Code 负责研究和初稿。

添加 n8n 将回复移动到 Slack 和 CRM 中，并添加 EmailBison 进行发送。

2. 选择一种类型的公司（一个周末）

他们的客户每个价值需要超过 1 万美元。

市场必须容纳 50,000 家以上的公司，而 10,000 家以下的公司最好逐个账户进行分析。

他们这边必须有人接听您预订的电话。

无聊的行业是最容易起步的。

建筑承包商的收件箱中只有供应商发票，没有其他内容，因此您的电子邮件会被阅读。

3. 绘制整个市场地图（一周，0 美元开始）

从 Apollo 的免费计划和 Google 地图中提取公司，然后将行业目录堆叠在顶部。

让人工智能阅读每家公司的网站，并根据客户的最佳客户对其进行评分。

告诉它什么是不合适的，并将任何东西减少到 80% 以下。

找到瀑布电子邮件：Icypeas→Prospeo→LeadMagic，与BlitzAPI的电话号码

然后使用 MillionVerifier 验证所有内容并通过 BounceBan 运行所有内容。

我们为一位客户在 Google 地图上绘制了 69,204 家企业的地图，并在 50 天内为他们预订了 53 场会议。

4. 设置发送（14 天）

在 Porkbun 上购买二级域名，并且永远不要从客户的真实域名发送。

在每个域上使用 SPF、DKIM 和 DMARC 从 ScaledMail 获取收件箱。

在发出一封冰冷的电子邮件之前，先将它们加热 14 天。

将每个收件箱每天最多发送 15 封冷电子邮件，并关闭开放式跟踪。

当您需要更多容量时，请添加收件箱，而不是推送现有的收件箱。

5. 写电子邮件（一个下午）

将其控制在 65 个字以下，如果要发送到 Outlook 收件箱，则控制在 40 个字以下。

首先介绍有关其业务的一个真实细节。

我们人工智能编写的第一行回复率达到了 0.27%。

使用潜在客户自己的项目和地点的活动达到了 14.5%。

接近他们可以接受的免费东西，比如样本列表或他们自己作品的模型。

在您确定每个版本不起作用之前，请先发送 1,000 多次。

6. 收到每条回复（同一天）

构建一个 n8n 流程，按意图标记每个回复并将好的回复发布到 Slack 中。

一分钟内回答，然后拿起电话给他们打电话。

一分钟内联系潜在客户可将转化率提高 391% (Velocify)。

在接下来的 2 天内提供 2 次优惠（“星期二 11 点还是星期三 2 点？”），而不是发送日历链接。

根据每个潜在客户的联系人来判断每个营销活动：低于 500 名就很好，大约 1,000 名需要调整，超过 2,000 名则意味着报价错误。

计算每月 3K 美元的数字：

1 个客户 = 3,000 美元
4 个客户 = 12,000 美元
10 个客户 = 3 万美元

GTM 工程相当于 2012 年数据科学的地位。

那些会后悔错过它的人现在就坐在特别提款权席位上。

没有人需要关于辞职的教程。

我们的 GTM 负责人针对 GTM 工程的各个部分编写了 40 页的指南。

评论“GTM”我会发送给您（必须关注）

title:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams
title_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot were all affected by the same outage. Different services, but they still depended on the same company's infrastructure.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.

full_text_en:
was reading @Acurast's new post about the Microsoft outage on November 12, and one part got me thinking.

Outlook, Teams and Copilot were all affected by the same outage. Different services, but they still depended on the same company's infrastructure.

Acurast points out something interesting here.

Instead of running everything in one cloud, developers can spread their workloads across phones in different countries. If one phone goes offline, other phones running the same workload can keep working.

Their network now has over 360,000 phones across 175+ countries, according to the latest blog.

But I think there's an important difference.

Acurast can't magically fix Outlook when Microsoft's servers go down. And an AI agent that needs Outlook's API would still have problems.

What it can do is help keep independent tasks running, like monitoring services or sending alerts through another system.

I'd actually like to see Acurast test this in public. Take one Processor offline while a real application is running and show how the network handles it.

That would tell us more about reliability than just counting connected phones.
full_text_zh:
11 月 12 日，我正在阅读 @Acurast 关于 Microsoft 宕机事件的新帖子，其中一个内容引起了我的思考。

Outlook、Teams 和 Copilot 均受到同一故障的影响。不同的服务，但它们仍然依赖于同一家公司的基础设施。

阿库拉斯特在这里指出了一些有趣的事情。

开发人员可以将工作负载分散到不同国家/地区的手机上，而不是在一个云中运行所有内容。如果一部电话离线，运行相同工作负载的其他电话可以继续工作。

根据最新博客，他们的网络目前在 175 多个国家/地区拥有超过 360,000 部电话。

但我认为有一个重要的区别。

当 Microsoft 的服务器出现故障时，Acurast 无法神奇地修复 Outlook。而需要 Outlook API 的 AI 代理仍然会遇到问题。

它可以做的是帮助保持独立任务的运行，例如监控服务或通过另一个系统发送警报。

我实际上希望看到 Acurast 公开测试这一点。在实际应用程序运行时使一个处理器离线并显示网络如何处理它。

这将告诉我们更多关于可靠性的信息，而不仅仅是计算连接的电话。

title:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arr
title_en:
“Delivered” can start an argument as easily as end one.

Imagine an agent ordering steel for a project. The shipment arrives. The buyer disputes whether it meets the specification.

Both agents have a reason to say they’re right. Who settles it?

That’s the lens I’m using for @GenLayer move to the @arbitrum stack.

The GenLayer Chain moved from ZK Stack to Nitro. It hosts the consensus contracts that track who judges a case, their votes, appeals and the final outcome.

The method of judgment stays the same. Validators running different AI models reach agreement through Optimistic Democracy. Intelligent contracts still execute in GenVM on validator nodes.

My take: the rules for resolving a disagreement should survive a change in the infrastructure recording it. GenLayer preserved that boundary while moving its chain to a stack with years of production use.

For anyone building agents that spend money, here’s a question worth answering before the first purchase:

What would your agent need to see before accepting “job done”?

两位经纪人都有理由说他们是对的。谁来解决？

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum

这就是我用于将 @GenLayer 迁移到 @arbitrum 堆栈的镜头。

GenLayer 链从 ZK Stack 迁移到 Nitro。它托管共识合约，跟踪案件的法官、他们的投票、上诉和最终结果。

判断方法保持不变。运行不同人工智能模型的验证者通过乐观民主达成一致。智能合约仍在验证器节点上的 GenVM 中执行。

我的看法是：解决分歧的规则应该在记录分歧的基础设施发生变化后继续存在。 GenLayer 保留了这一边界，同时将其链转移到具有多年生产使用的堆栈中。

在接受“工作完成”之前，您的代理人需要看到什么？

title_en:
Every protocol has an origin story. Most are technical. This one is legal.

@kstellana built his previous project. Everything was going well until a serious legal dispute hit. He had no court to go to. No system built for the speed and scale of what he was building.

That frustration became @GenLayer.

In this episode with @HenriArslanian, Albert explains the exact moment he realized traditional legal systems cannot handle the agentic economy. AI agents will make millions of deals. They need a court that moves at their speed.

The clip below captures the origin. The problem that started it all.

What legal dispute in your own journey made you realize the system is broken?
full_text_en:

@kstellana built his previous project. Everything was going well until a serious legal dispute hit. He had no court to go to. No system built for the speed and scale of what he was building.

That frustration became @GenLayer.

In this episode with @HenriArslanian, Albert explains the exact moment he realized traditional legal systems cannot handle the agentic economy. AI agents will make millions of deals. They need a court that moves at their speed.

The clip below captures the origin. The problem that started it all.

What legal dispute in your own journey made you realize the system is broken?
full_text_zh:
每个协议都有一个起源故事。大多数都是技术性的。这是合法的。

title_en:
A court does not run its own power grid. GenLayer, the adjudication layer for AI agents, follows a similar split.

Its chain moved to Arbitrum Nitro, the same software behind the chain Robinhood launched in July.

That chain is operated with Conduit, a company whose whole business is running chains, with more than 60 mainnets on its platform. The GenLayer team keeps its hands on the protocol.

I like that division of labour. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts are where GenLayer's judgment lives, and the move leaves them as they were. Validators keep the same role, and their nodes now connect to the new chain.

The next phase of the Bradbury testnet went live the same day. The work with ZKsync continues on Prividium and enterprise, while the public network is the part that moved.

@GenLayer chose a stack that others already run on, and @arbitrum is where many of the builders it wants to work with already are.

Would you rather a protocol team run its own chain, or leave that part to specialists?

full_text_en:
A court does not run its own power grid. GenLayer, the adjudication layer for AI agents, follows a similar split.

Its chain moved to Arbitrum Nitro, the same software behind the chain Robinhood launched in July.

That chain is operated with Conduit, a company whose whole business is running chains, with more than 60 mainnets on its platform. The GenLayer team keeps its hands on the protocol.

I like that division of labour. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts are where GenLayer's judgment lives, and the move leaves them as they were. Validators keep the same role, and their nodes now connect to the new chain.

The next phase of the Bradbury testnet went live the same day. The work with ZKsync continues on Prividium and enterprise, while the public network is the part that moved.

@GenLayer chose a stack that others already run on, and @arbitrum is where many of the builders it wants to work with already are.

Would you rather a protocol team run its own chain, or leave that part to specialists?
full_text_zh:
法院不运营自己的电网。 GenLayer 是人工智能代理的裁决层，也遵循类似的划分。

它的链转移到 Arbitrum Nitro，这与 7 月份推出的 Robinhood 链背后的软件相同。

该链由 Conduit 运营，该公司的全部业务都是运营链，其平台上有 60 多个主网。 GenLayer 团队负责掌握该协议。

我喜欢这种分工。乐观民主、GenVM 和智能合约是 GenLayer 的判断所在，而此举让它们保持原样。验证者保持相同的角色，他们的节点现在连接到新链。

布拉德伯里测试网的下一阶段于同一天上线。 ZKsync 的工作在 Prividium 和企业上继续进行，而公共网络是移动的部分。

@GenLayer 选择了其他人已经运行的堆栈，而 @arbitrum 是它想要使用的许多构建器已经所在的位置。

What actually happens inside an AI agent?

An AI agent is more than an LLM connected to a prompt. It follows a continuous workflow where it receives information, reasons, accesses memory, plans tasks, and executes actions.

Here's a breakdown of the architecture behind modern AI agents.

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 & 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

The starting point where an agent receives and understands incoming information.

→ User text and instructions

→ API calls

→ Sensor data

→ Events and triggers

02 — 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗘 / 𝗟𝗟𝗠

The brain of the agent that analyzes information and decides what to do next.

→ Chain-of-Thought

→ ReAct

→ Plan-and-Execute

→ Decision-making

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

Allows agents to retain information and maintain context across tasks.

→ Short-term: Conversation context and working state.

→ Long-term: Vector stores and episodic memory.

→ Learned patterns: Previously stored information.

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

Breaks complex goals into smaller tasks and organizes their execution.

→ Goal decomposition

→ Task sequencing

→ Step-by-step execution

→ Progress tracking

Example:

→ Step 1: Understand the goal.

→ Step 2: Break it into subtasks.

→ Step 3: Execute each step.

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

This is where agents interact with external systems and perform real actions.

→ Model Context Protocol (MCP)

→ API calls

→ Code execution

→ Database queries

→ File system

→ External services like GitHub

Results are sent back to the reasoning engine for further processing.

06 — 𝗚𝗨𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

Keeps agent operations within defined security boundaries.

→ Permission controls

→ Approval gates

→ Content filtering

→ Rate limits

→ Human-in-the-loop checkpoints

07 — 𝗢𝗕𝗦𝗘𝗥𝗩𝗔𝗕𝗜𝗟𝗜𝗧𝗬 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

Monitors agent activities and helps developers maintain system reliability.

→ Execution tracing

→ Error monitoring

→ Workflow tracking

→ Performance monitoring

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗨𝗔𝗟 𝗔𝗚𝗘𝗡𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗙𝗟𝗢𝗪:

Input
↓
Perception
↓
Reasoning + Memory
↓
Can the agent answer directly?

→ YES: Generate output.

→ NO: Move to planning and tool execution.

Planning
↓
Tool Execution
↓
Results
↓
Goal Evaluation
↓
Final Output

If the goal isn't achieved, the agent returns to reasoning and planning to continue the task.

𝗧𝗛𝗘 𝗞𝗘𝗬 𝗟𝗘𝗦𝗦𝗢𝗡:

An AI agent isn't just a language model. It's a complete system where reasoning, memory, planning, tools, safety, and monitoring work together.

Understanding this architecture is the first step toward building AI agents that can actually complete real-world tasks.

人工智能代理内部到底发生了什么？

AI 代理不仅仅是连接到提示的法学硕士。它遵循连续的工作流程，接收信息、推理、访问内存、计划任务并执行操作。

以下是现代人工智能代理背后的架构细分。

𝗛𝗘𝗥𝗘’𝗦 𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗜𝗧 𝗪𝗢𝗥𝗞𝗦:

01 — 𝗜𝗡𝗣𝗨𝗧 & 𝗣𝗘𝗥𝗖𝗘𝗣𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

代理接收并理解传入信息的起点。

→ 用户文本和说明

→ API 调用

→ 传感器数据

→ 事件和触发器

02 — 𝗥𝗘𝗔𝗦𝗢𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗘𝗡𝗚𝗜𝗡𝗘 / 𝗟𝗟𝗠

智能体的大脑，负责分析信息并决定下一步该做什么。

→ 思想链

→ 反应

→ 计划与执行

→ 决策

03 — 𝗠𝗘𝗠𝗢𝗥𝗬 𝗦𝗬𝗦𝗧𝗘𝗠

允许代理保留信息并维护跨任务的上下文。

→ 短期：对话情境和工作状态。

→ 长期：向量存储和情景记忆。

→ 学习模式：之前存储的信息。

04 — 𝗣𝗟𝗔𝗡𝗡𝗜𝗡𝗚 𝗠𝗢𝗗𝗨𝗟𝗘

将复杂的目标分解为较小的任务并组织其执行。

→ 目标分解

→ 任务排序

→ 逐步执行

→ 进度追踪

例子：

→ 第 1 步：了解目标。

→ 第 2 步：将其分解为子任务。

→ 步骤3：执行每一步。

05 — 𝗧𝗢𝗢𝗟 𝗘𝗫𝗘𝗖𝗨𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 / 𝗔𝗖𝗧𝗜𝗢𝗡 𝗟𝗔𝗬𝗘𝗥

这是代理与外部系统交互并执行实际操作的地方。

→ 模型上下文协议 (MCP)

→ API 调用

→ 代码执行

→ 数据库查询

→ 文件系统

→ GitHub 等外部服务

结果被发送回推理引擎进行进一步处理。

06 — 𝗚𝗨𝗔𝗥𝗗𝗥𝗔𝗜𝗟𝗦 & 𝗦𝗔𝗙𝗘𝗧𝗬

将代理操作保持在定义的安全边界内。

→ 权限控制

→ 审批门

→ 内容过滤

→ 速率限制

→ 人机交互检查点

→ 性能监控

title:
Why would GenLayer run on two paths at once?

Picture two customers walking in on the same day.

The first is a small te
title_en:
Why would GenLayer run on two paths at once?

Picture two customers walking in on the same day.

The first is a small team building an AI agent app. They want a public network, open tooling and builders already nearby. For them, GenLayer's public network now runs on the @arbitrum stack. Nitro is built around Geth, so normal Ethereum tools work as they are. Robinhood runs its own chain on the same software.

The second is a group of banks. They want to settle contracts between themselves, and that cannot sit on a public chain. For them, @GenLayer keeps working with Matter Labs on Prividium, a private, permissioned version.

Two different needs, same engine. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts work the same way. What changed was only where the contracts touch the chain: the bridge, the Ethereum link and gas handling.

So the move does not shrink the plan. It gives each customer the right door. And Bradbury going live on the new stack the same day shows it is already running.

Which door do you think brings in more builders first, public or private?

full_text_en:
Why would GenLayer run on two paths at once?

Picture two customers walking in on the same day.

The first is a small team building an AI agent app. They want a public network, open tooling and builders already nearby. For them, GenLayer's public network now runs on the @arbitrum stack. Nitro is built around Geth, so normal Ethereum tools work as they are. Robinhood runs its own chain on the same software.

The second is a group of banks. They want to settle contracts between themselves, and that cannot sit on a public chain. For them, @GenLayer keeps working with Matter Labs on Prividium, a private, permissioned version.

Two different needs, same engine. Optimistic Democracy, GenVM and intelligent contracts work the same way. What changed was only where the contracts touch the chain: the bridge, the Ethereum link and gas handling.

So the move does not shrink the plan. It gives each customer the right door. And Bradbury going live on the new stack the same day shows it is already running.

Which door do you think brings in more builders first, public or private?
full_text_zh:
为什么 GenLayer 会同时在两条路径上运行？

想象一下同一天走进来的两个顾客。

第一个是一个构建人工智能代理应用程序的小团队。他们想要一个公共网络、开放工具和已经在附近的构建器。对于他们来说，GenLayer 的公共网络现在在 @arbitrum 堆栈上运行。 Nitro 是围绕 Geth 构建的，因此普通的以太坊工具可以按原样工作。 Robinhood 在同一软件上运行自己的链。

第二个是银行集团。他们想要在彼此之间结算合同，而这不能放在公共链上。对于他们来说，@GenLayer 继续与 Matter Labs 合作开发 Prividium（一个私有的、经过许可的版本）。

两种不同的需求，相同的引擎。乐观民主、GenVM 和智能合约的工作原理是一样的。改变的只是合约接触链的地方：桥、以太坊链接和天然气处理。

因此此举并没有缩小计划。它为每个客户提供了正确的大门。 Bradbury 于同一天在新堆栈上上线，表明它已经在运行。

您认为哪扇门首先会吸引更多的建筑商，是公共的还是私人的？

Developer ILFforever
title_en:
👻 YO-KAI WATCH 4++ RECOMPILATION brings 4K, ultrawide, high FPS and native Linux support to PC! 🎮🔥

Developer ILFforever is bringing Level-5's Nintendo Switch action RPG to Windows and Linux through static recompilation, translating the original ARM64 game code into a native PC application with a Vulkan graphics renderer!

🔥 FEATURES:

✅ NATIVE WINDOWS & LINUX! Including a Linux AppImage launcher — no Switch emulator required!

✅ 4K & ULTRAWIDE! Supports 1080p, 1440p, 4K and 21:9/32:9 aspect ratios!

✅ HIGH FRAME RATES! 30, 60, 120, 144 FPS and uncapped options!

✅ DLSS & FSR! Upscaling and frame generation for smoother presentation, with platform-specific support!

✅ ENHANCED GRAPHICS! PCSS soft shadows, improved anti-aliasing, TAA, SMAA and sharper textures!

✅ MOD SUPPORT! Includes compatibility with the fan-made English translation patch!

✅ MODERN CONTROLS! Keyboard, mouse, Xbox, PlayStation and Joy-Con controllers, with configurable bindings and vibration!

✅ DEDICATED LAUNCHER! Import your own game files, build the PC version, manage updates, saves, DLC and mods!

🔥 BETA v1.5.0 — PLAYABLE BUT UNFINISHED!

The opening, several locations and late-game battles have been tested. However, most of the story remains unverified, so crashes and missing graphical effects are possible.

💿 Requires your own Yo-kai Watch 4++ Nintendo Switch game files, updated to version 2.2.0.

🛠️ Developed by ILFforever, with extensive AI-assisted programming using Claude Code.

title:
something people might overlook when using AI agents for trading is the paperwork that comes after every transaction.

@
title_en:
something people might overlook when using AI agents for trading is the paperwork that comes after every transaction.

@meetmotes is exploring autonomous agents for financial markets, but i think there's another part of the experience worth discussing.

imagine an agent making trades across different markets throughout the week.

after some time, how easily can the user find out what happened?

which asset was bought or sold, when the transaction happened, what price was executed, how much was paid in fees, and what the final position looks like.

these details matter when reviewing performance, tracking a portfolio, or preparing financial records.

i wouldn't want users to dig through dozens of transaction links just to understand what their own agent has been doing.

a clear, downloadable activity history could make a big difference.

automation should save users time, not create another administrative headache.

a good AI agent should make the activity easier to manage, even after the trade is finished.

一段时间后，用户如何容易地发现发生了什么？

购买或出售哪些资产、交易何时发生、执行价格是多少、支付了多少费用以及最终头寸是什么样的。

在审查绩效、跟踪投资组合或准备财务记录时，这些细节很重要。

清晰、可下载的活动历史记录可能会产生很大的影响。

自动化应该节省用户时间，而不是造成另一个管理难题。

一个好的人工智能代理应该使活动更容易管理，即使在交易完成后也是如此。

title:
Here's how hackers are now using AI to attack companies, according to a new Google report:

1. A software company releas
title_en:
Here's how hackers are now using AI to attack companies, according to a new Google report:

1. A software company releases a security update

2. An AI agent compares the old code to the new code

3. It figures out exactly which weakness was just fixed

4. It writes an attack for that weakness

5. It hits every company that hasn't installed the update yet

No human needed at any step.

Google found one of these tools, called "exploit_agent," sitting on an exposed hacker server.

Its verdict: "The era of autonomous attacks has arrived."
title_zh:
根据谷歌的一份新报告，黑客现在如何利用人工智能来攻击公司：

1.某软件公司发布安全更新

2. AI 代理将旧代码与新代码进行比较

3.它准确地指出哪个弱点刚刚被修复

4. 针对该弱点编写攻击

5.它会影响所有尚未安装更新的公司
